For actual fine-layer cells with common origin, endpoint set and radius C ≥ 2, an opposing cell corner lying on a whole reference side is that side’s start, midpoint or end. Only the reference layer k is assumed to satisfy 50000000 ≤ k; the opposing layer h has no separate lower bound. Both actual fineLayerIndices memberships are required. No distinct-cell or belt hypothesis is imposed.

Source: Section 11, lines 299–306 and 352–356. The whole reference side is expressed by the unsplit cellFanStart and cellFanEnd, and its midpoint is midpoint ℝ. Closed-layer locality and adjacent fine-scale ratios establish the common half-side mesh.
Independently formalized from the cited manuscript; no upstream Lean source or proof text is reused.
Proves pairwise disjointness of the actual half-open layers D_k = N_(k+1) \ N_k for arbitrary origin, finite endpoint set and natural radius, including an empty endpoint set.
Source: Section 11, lines 160–177. This is a consequence of the existing nesting of the actual dyadic neighborhoods. It does not assert disjointness of their closures.
Independently formalized from the cited manuscript; no upstream Lean source or proof text is reused.
For arbitrary origin, finite endpoint set and natural radius, proves N_(k₀) disjoint from D_k whenever k₀ ≤ k. The equality case k = k₀ is included; an empty endpoint set is allowed.
Source: Section 11, lines 169–177. Both sets are the actual half-open neighborhood and layer, and the only index assumption is k₀ ≤ k.
Independently formalized from the cited manuscript; no upstream Lean source or proof text is reused.

For a nonempty finite endpoint set, radius C ≥ 2 and arbitrary lower index k₀, every point outside N_(k₀) belongs to a unique actual layer D_k with k₀ ≤ k. The least neighborhood index K containing the point yields k = K − 1.
Source: Section 11, lines 160–177. Existing neighborhood exhaustion supplies existence; nesting makes K > k₀, and actual half-open layer disjointness supplies uniqueness.

Source: Section 11, lines 160–177. The initial neighborhood and the later layers form an exact cover of the plane; no claim about pairwise disjoint closed birth regions is made.

For arbitrary origin, finite endpoint set and natural radius, an actual dyadic cell of exponent ℓ lies in the actual half-open layer D_k whenever ℓ ≤ k and its index belongs to fineLayerIndices o k ℓ Z C. No endpoint nonemptiness, radius lower bound or late-layer hypothesis is imposed.

Source: Section 11, lines 154–160 and 173–181. This shared cell-containment theorem follows from the existing exact union of finer half-open cells. It replaces repeated local containment proofs without changing the previously established conclusions.
